post.headline: Notification addresses stay private
post.subtext: Recipients and staff can use Notifications to choose Hush Line inbox notifications, email notifications, and whether encrypted tip contents are included in email.
post.image_alt_text: Social image showing a light-mode desktop Hush Line Settings page on the Notifications tab. The screen shows Tip Notifications turned on, a Recipients section saying notification recipient addresses stay private and are never shown on the public tip line, enabled recipient addresses with PGP keys configured, and an Add Recipient button. The asset supports a myth-versus-reality message that staff alerts can stay private while recipients choose inbox and email notification settings.

social.bluesky:
Myth: email notifications expose staff addresses.

Reality: Hush Line notification recipient addresses stay private. Recipients and staff can choose inbox notices, email notices, and whether encrypted tip contents are included in email.
social.linkedin:
Myth: adding email notifications means exposing staff addresses on your public tip line.

Reality: Hush Line notification recipient addresses stay private and are never shown on your public tip line.

For a shared recipient account, recipients and staff can choose Hush Line inbox notifications, email notifications, and whether encrypted tip contents are included in email. They can also add more than one notification recipient, each with its own delivery address and PGP key.

Use Notifications to decide who gets alerts, what goes into email, and what stays in the Hush Line inbox.

post.rationale: Selected the only provided recipient-shared candidate. The notification topic has appeared before, so this post avoids older angles about quick alerts, forwarding, or setup timing and focuses on a different repeatable workflow decision: adding private notification recipients while choosing inbox notifications, email notifications, and encrypted tip content in email.
